title: When a Highway Robot Chef Fails at Making Ramen
key_facts: A 24-hour unmanned ramen robot at the Gapyeong Service Area on South Korea's Seoul-Yangyang Expressway showed a red "Failure" alert after it dropped a block of noodles while cooking green onion ramen.
A photo of the mess, with noodles and soup powder on the counter and floor, went viral online last week.
The robot developer says a failure alert has appeared only once or twice so far, and on-site staff give a refund.
Cooking takes about 4 minutes 30 to 50 seconds, and up to four bowls can be made at once.
The Seoul-bound store opened last month on a two-month trial; robot ramen sells about 60 bowls a day on weekdays and 140 at weekends.
Per Korea Expressway Corporation data cited in the article, service-area cooking robots grew from 3 stores in 2021 to 103 last year.
Page carries a note that the article was translated by AI.
quote_evidence: It appears to be an unexpected incident caused when a 24-hour unmanned "robot chef" dropped a block of ramen noodles midway through cooking a customer's order of green onion ramen.
We process such instances as 'failures' and display them on the screen.
Errors can still occur when orders flood in all at once, so it is still in the early stages of checking and improving problems.
why_it_matters_hint: Shows cooking robots spreading quickly in places short of night staff, with early glitches.
event_date: Failure photo went viral the week before 7 Oct 2026; exact date not stated
notes: Fulltext fetch held only page links; read the article body from the SBS page data directly. The page says it was machine-translated and credits a photo to the Ruliweb forum and Yonhap News. Event is older than 6 Oct.
